subject: Inference SLO + deployment action plan (summary & next steps)
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 24 Jun 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Inference SLO + deployment action plan (summary & next steps)

Thanks again for the call earlier — good alignment overall. Below is a concise recap of the problems you described, the goals we discussed, and proposed next steps so everyone has the same reference. I copied our infra leads (Karthik, Neha) for the technical follow-up.

Key pain points agreed on:
- Intermittent latency spikes during morning batch windows (06:00–09:00 PT) causing p95 breaches and downstream API throttling.
- Cost unpredictability when traffic bursts hit (token bill in last quarter spiked ~2.6x).
- Need for PHI-safe hosting and strong KMS/HSM controls for keys.

Target goals you stated:
- p95 inference latency target: 300 ms (for typical prompt sizes up to ~512 tokens).
- Stable throughput during peak: sustained 80 qps with 20% headroom for bursts.
- Keep per-token serving cost within ~30% of current baseline while improving latency.

Technical constraints and model notes from call:
- Primary model candidate: Llama2-13B (open) for current QA pipeline; planning a later run with a 70B variant for higher-quality responses.
- Sequence lengths average 420 tokens; tails up to ~2k on rare jobs.
- On-prem/VPC requirement for PHI-sensitive workloads — likely Private deployment.

Initial topology & optimization ideas (high level)
- Private (VPC) deployment behind customer-controlled ingress + Redwood private control plane.
- Quantized model path (4-bit) for the 13B candidate to hit latency/cost targets; reserve full-precision variant for fallbacks.
- KV / prefix caching for repeated system prompts and long-context reuse.
- Autoscaling policy tuned to p95 SLOs with a conservative burst buffer.

Attachments included: inference_sla_template.pdf (SLA draft), sentry_deploy_topology_v1.drawio (sketch).

Proposed next steps (owners & rough dates):
1) Security checklist & KMS/HSM requirements — Sentry action: share any existing procurement/security docs (SOC2, KMS spec) by Tues 6/27 — Owner: Sentry (Olivia).
2) PoC kickoff (small-scale private cluster + 13B quantized): Redwood to provide topology options and cost estimate by Thu 6/30 — Owner: Redwood (Karthik).
3) Schedule technical kickoff (90-minute deep-dive) week of 7/8 — Owner: joint.
4) HubSpot/Deal update and PO / procurement questions to be tracked on RDW-5467 — Owner: Stephanie.

If that matches your expectations, I’ll queue Karthik to draft the PoC topology and cost envelope.

Thanks,

--

Quick technical follow-up and a proposed PoC topology based on the targets (p95=300ms, sustained 80 qps):

Summary of assumptions:
- Working model: Llama2-13B quantized to 4-bit for the primary path; 70B reserved as a fall-back.
- Average request: 420 tokens output + 50 token prompt; budgeting for KV reuse reduces typical compute by ~12–18% on repeated prompts.

PoC topology (initial sketch):
- Private VPC deployment with 3 GPU workers (H100 equivalent or 4xA100 split across 2 nodes) for the quantized 13B path to meet latency headroom.
- One dedicated node for a smaller variant (e.g., 7B) to handle overflow and serve as fast fallback.
- KV cache layer (Redis-backed prefix cache) in the VPC to reduce per-request compute for repeated contexts.
- Batching: dynamic batching with a target max batch latency of 30 ms; keep batch windows short (<10 ms) during p95-sensitive routes.
- Autoscaler: reactive + predictive policy using traffic histograms from your logs; keep a 20% buffer for morning burst.

Estimate (very rough) for PoC infra footprint and expected performance:
- Expected p95: ~220–320 ms depending on prompt tail; p99 may spike to ~900 ms during extreme tails unless we route to fallback.
- Sustained throughput: 60–100 qps depending on batching; planning for 80 qps with headroom recommended.
- Rough monthly infra cost (private): estimate $18k–$30k depending on instance choice and reserved vs on-demand. We’ll refine with exact instance types once we confirm allowed hardware and HSM requirements.

Security/KMS: Redwood supports customer-managed keys via integrations with major KMS providers; HSM-backed flows are supported for Private deployments (we’ll confirm architecture for your vendor).

Next technical deliverables I’ll produce by Thu 6/30:
- PoC topology diagram (drawio) + instance sizing.
- Expected perf/cost envelope with 3 scenarios (conservative / expected / aggressive).
- Canary & rollback plan for model fallback.

— Karthik
